learningObjectives: Explain why the neuronal interior is negative relative to the exterior at rest.
Distinguish the roles of leak channels, concentration gradients and Na+/K+-ATPase.
Predict how changes in extracellular potassium alter excitability.
Relate resting potential to threshold and clinical network stability.

anatomy.label: Ion gradients
anatomy.detail: Sodium is concentrated outside the neuron and potassium inside. These gradients store potential energy across the membrane.
anatomy.clinical: Rapid changes in serum sodium or potassium can alter excitability and produce confusion, weakness or seizures.

anatomy.label: Potassium leak channels
anatomy.detail: At rest, potassium leak channels allow more potassium movement than sodium movement, pulling voltage toward the potassium equilibrium potential.
anatomy.clinical: Channel expression helps set how responsive a neuron is to incoming signals.

anatomy.label: Na+/K+-ATPase
anatomy.detail: The pump uses ATP to move three sodium ions out and two potassium ions in, preserving gradients over time.
anatomy.clinical: Hypoxia and metabolic failure compromise the pump, causing ionic collapse and cellular swelling.

anatomy.label: Intracellular anions
anatomy.detail: Large negatively charged proteins and phosphates remain trapped inside the cell and contribute to intracellular negativity.
anatomy.clinical: Cell injury can disturb osmotic and ionic balance even without a primary channel disorder.

interaction.title: Resting Membrane Potential sequence
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence to see how the system changes over time.

stages.label: Separate
stages.text: ATP-dependent transport maintains sodium outside and potassium inside.

stages.label: Leak
stages.text: Potassium moves down its concentration gradient through leak channels.

stages.label: Balance
stages.text: Electrical attraction opposes further potassium loss.

stages.label: Stabilise
stages.text: The membrane settles near a negative resting voltage, ready to respond.

quizBank.question: Which ion has the greatest influence on a typical neuron’s resting membrane potential?
quizBank.explanation: Resting conductance is usually dominated by potassium leak channels.

quizBank.question: What is the main role of Na+/K+-ATPase at rest?
options: Maintain sodium and potassium gradients over time
quizBank.explanation: The pump preserves the concentration gradients that support membrane voltage.

quizBank.question: Why is the inside of a resting neuron relatively negative?
options: Selective ion permeability and retained intracellular anions
Because electrons flow down the axon
Because all sodium leaves the cell
Because the nucleus is negatively charged
quizBank.explanation: Selective permeability and fixed intracellular anions produce relative intracellular negativity.

quizBank.question: What usually happens if extracellular potassium rises substantially?
options: The resting voltage becomes less negative
quizBank.explanation: A reduced potassium gradient tends to depolarise the membrane and alter excitability.

quizBank.question: “Resting” membrane potential means the neuron is:
options: Not firing an action potential but still metabolically active
quizBank.explanation: Resting neurons actively maintain gradients and receive continuous input.
